result.summary: Pausanias gives the Tegeans' account of their district's name, their parishes and their local renown. He then describes the great temple of Athene Alea, its history, orders of columns, architect Scopas and the sculptures on its gables.

scenes.title: Tegea's name and renown
scenes.summary: The Tegeans explain their origins, parishes and founder, and list their famous deeds, from the Calydonian boar to victories over the Lacedaemonians.

scenes.title: The temple of Athene Alea
scenes.summary: The old temple built by Aleus burned down, and a larger temple by Scopas replaced it, with Doric, Corinthian and Ionic columns.
scenes.stakes: The old temple is lost entirely to fire.

scenes.title: The gable sculptures
scenes.summary: The front gable shows the Calydonian boar hunt and the rear gable shows Telephus fighting Achilles.

notable_quotes.reason: Pausanias praises the Tegean temple as the finest in the Peloponnese.

analysis.text: Local pride: Tegea ties its identity to heroic myth and to victories over Sparta.
The temple, rebuilt after a fire in the 4th century BC with Scopas as architect, shows the era's art and wealth, combining three column orders.

fun_facts.text: Pausanias dates the fire by the Athenian archon and an Olympic victor, showing how Greeks reckoned dates.

language_notes.text: "Parishes" translates the Greek divisions (demes or districts) of Tegea; here it means administrative districts, not church parishes.
Dipæa was a battle fought in Arcadia in the early fifth century BC, in which the Tegeans and other Arcadians faced Sparta.
The Heraclidæ, descendants of Hercules, tried to return to the Peloponnese; Echemus of Tegea is said to have killed Hyllus, Hercules' son, in single combat.
The fire is dated by the Athenian archon and the Olympiad, the usual Greek dating method. "The course" means the foot-race.
Althæa was Meleager's mother, and her brothers, the sons of Thestius, took part in the Calydonian hunt; Meleager later killed them in a quarrel over the boar's spoils.
Telephus, king of Mysia, was wounded by Achilles' spear while fighting the Greeks on the plain of the Caicus river; the wound was later healed by rust from the same spear.

context_notes.text: Atalanta was a famed huntress; in the Calydonian boar hunt, Greek heroes gathered to kill a monstrous boar sent by Artemis.
Athene Alea was Tegea's chief goddess, and her sanctuary was a major religious centre in Arcadia.
Scopas of Paros was a leading fourth-century BC sculptor and architect, known for work on the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus.

literary_notes.text: Pausanias praises the temple as surpassing every other in the Peloponnese, emphasizing local pride and the building's grandeur.
The long list of heroes arranged around the boar gives a visual sense of the sculpture and lends the hunt epic grandeur.
